Driving Document

Tableau Knowledge Demo Charter

Goals, evidence standards, PRD alignment, claim boundaries, and review criteria.

This document is the reference point for designing, evaluating, and presenting Tableau Knowledge demos. Use it when choosing scenarios, writing prompts, reviewing a demo, or deciding whether a new capability strengthens the story.

Product Thesis

AI systems produce more accurate, consistent, and explainable answers when business definitions, scope, relationships, and provenance are explicit in a governed Knowledge Graph.

The demo must show more than an agent calling a Tableau API. It must show a material improvement in the quality and trustworthiness of an answer because Tableau Knowledge supplied organization-specific context that the agent otherwise did not have.

Demo Goal

Prove that Tableau Knowledge turns an ambiguous business question into a governed answer by giving the agent:

DefinitionThe organization's approved business meaning.
CalculationThe exact formula or usage rule, when one exists.
ScopeThe asset or domain in which that meaning applies.
EvidenceRelationships and provenance the agent can explain.

The audience should leave understanding that Tableau Knowledge reduces reliance on generic model knowledge and prevents an agent from silently choosing a plausible but incorrect interpretation.

PRD Outcomes Demonstrated

PRD outcome What the demo must show
Reduce hallucinations The agent refuses to invent a definition or substitute an unsupported proxy.
Consistent definitions The answer uses the semantic statement stored in the Knowledge Graph.
Explainability The agent identifies the definition, relationship, and source supporting its answer.
Connected knowledge A business concept is connected to the Tableau asset where it applies.
Open agent access An external agent retrieves governed Knowledge through Tableau MCP.
Contextual retrieval The answer distinguishes organization-specific scope from generic industry meaning.
Trust A reviewer can inspect the evidence behind each material claim.

Primary Demonstration Pattern

Use a controlled before-and-after comparison with the same substantive business question.

Without Tableau Knowledge

The agent may recognize common terminology, but it cannot establish which definition the organization approved, whether a generic definition applies, where the definition applies, or what evidence supports it. The correct behavior is to acknowledge missing context instead of presenting an unsupported answer as fact.

With Tableau Knowledge

The agent retrieves the governed definition and follows graph relationships to establish where it applies. Its answer includes the definition, formula or rule, applicable scope, and provenance. The difference must be caused by graph evidence, not by changing the question or giving away the answer in the prompt.

Current Anchor Scenario

The reference scenario asks what ACV means for Sales Cloud and how it is calculated.

  • ACV means Annual Contract Value.
  • It is the net increase in revenue from a customer compared with the prior year.
  • It represents new growth, not the full contract value.
  • The governed calculation is [Current Year Contract Value] - [Prior Year Contract Value].
  • The ACV semantic context has a DESCRIBES relationship to the Sales Cloud published data source.

This scenario is effective because ACV has plausible alternatives. A model could confuse it with total contract value or related concepts such as AOV and NNAOV. Tableau Knowledge resolves that ambiguity with an explicit definition and graph scope.

Evidence Chain

  1. Discovery: Semantic search locates the governed concept.
  2. Meaning: A semantic statement supplies the definition and formula.
  3. Scope: A graph relationship establishes which asset the context describes.
  4. Answer: The agent separates graph-supported facts from assumptions or gaps.
Stage ACV evidence
Discovery search-knowledge-nodes returns the ACV semantic-context node.
Meaning The statement defines ACV and contains the exact calculation.
Scope get-knowledge-node-relationships returns a DESCRIBES edge to Sales Cloud.
Answer The agent states the governed definition, calculation, scope, and provenance.

Core Messages

  • Tableau Knowledge provides governed meaning, not merely technical metadata.
  • The graph tells an agent both what a concept means and where that meaning applies.
  • Graph relationships make the answer explainable instead of relying on opaque reasoning.
  • The agent can distinguish related metrics without silently selecting a proxy.
  • MCP makes governed context available outside a single Tableau experience.
The value is not that the agent found a field called ACV. Tableau Knowledge tells the agent what ACV means here, how this organization calculates it, where that definition applies, and what evidence supports the answer.

Non-Goals and Claim Boundaries

The current demo proves governed contextual retrieval. Do not claim that it provides:

  • General natural-language-to-SQL generation.
  • Arbitrary analytical answers over underlying business data.
  • Automatic graph discovery or active-graph selection.
  • Complete conflict resolution across every source and scope.
  • Trust guarantees not present in returned graph metadata.
  • A successful data query when only metadata and semantic context were retrieved.

Demo Design Principles

Keep the question constantSupplying a required graph ID is an implementation necessity, not a new business question.
Make improvement causalThe improved answer must depend on information returned from Tableau Knowledge.
Prefer ambiguous termsMultiple plausible meanings make the value of governed context visible.
Show the evidencePause on the semantic statement and graph relationship, not only the polished answer.
Reward abstentionIf the graph does not establish a claim, the agent should say so.
Separate metadata from analyticsNever imply underlying data execution when only definitions were retrieved.

Success Criteria

  • The baseline does not assert an unsupported organization-specific definition or formula.
  • The Knowledge path uses semantic search as its first discovery step.
  • The answer reproduces the governed definition and formula accurately.
  • The answer establishes scope through graph evidence rather than prompt inference.
  • The answer makes its provenance understandable to the audience.
  • No unsupported proxy metric is introduced and no write operation occurs.
  • The presenter can explain which PRD outcome each proof point demonstrates.

Evaluation Questions

  1. What can the agent establish with Knowledge that it cannot establish without it?
  2. Is that difference visible and meaningful to a business audience?
  3. Which exact graph evidence supports the final answer?
  4. Does the graph establish both meaning and scope?
  5. Could generic model knowledge alone produce the improved answer?
  6. Does the prompt accidentally reveal the answer?
  7. Are we claiming analytical execution when only metadata was retrieved?
  8. What should the agent do if required evidence is missing?
  9. Which PRD objective or pain point does each stage demonstrate?
  10. Can the scenario be reproduced and evaluated consistently?

Current Constraints

  • Knowledge retrieval tools currently require an explicit graph ID.
  • The ACV graph is 16ca1f04951844e2aeb26ca744d41e85 on tk-demo-tdp1.
  • Graphless prompts should request the graph ID without unrelated metadata fallback.
  • The anchor search result already contains the ACV statement, so a separate statement lookup is redundant and should not be part of the demo route.
  • Live evals require a Tableau environment and an LLM endpoint.

Future Evolution

  • Resolve the active graph without requiring the user to provide an ID.
  • Demonstrate scope selection across conflicting definitions.
  • Prioritize a more specific definition over a broader one.
  • Compare authoritative assets with lower-trust alternatives.
  • Trace lineage from a metric to source fields and downstream consumers.
  • Demonstrate impact analysis before changing a definition or calculation.
  • Add analytical questions when supported natural-language query execution is available.
